title: VF Corporation Completes Sale of Dickies® to Bluestar Alliance
summary: November 12, 2025 4:10pm EST - DENVER & NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- VF Corporation (NYSE: VFC), a global leader in branded lifestyle apparel, footwear and accessories,…
body_text: VF Corporation Completes Sale of Dickies® to Bluestar Alliance Download as PDF November 12, 2025 4:10pm EST DENVER & NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- VF Corporation (NYSE: VFC), a global leader in branded lifestyle apparel, footwear and accessories, announced that it has successfully closed the previously announced transaction to sell the Dickies® brand to Bluestar Alliance LLC, a leading global brand management firm, for an aggregate base purchase price of $600 million in cash subject to customary adjustments. About VF VF Corporation is a portfolio of leading outdoor, active and workwear brands, including The North Face ®, Vans ®, and Timberland ®. VF is committed to providing consumers with innovative products that are rooted in performance and elevated design, while delivering sustainable and long-term value for its employees, communities, and shareholders. For more information, please visit vfc.com. About Bluestar Alliance, LLC Founded in 2006 by Joseph Gabbay and Ralph Gindi, Bluestar Alliance is a global brand management leader, overseeing a portfolio of premium fashion and lifestyle brands generating more than $13 billion in global retail sales. Bluestar Alliance is recognized for transforming iconic consumer names into dynamic, best-in-class lifestyle brands with worldwide reach. Its portfolio includes Off-White™, Palm Angels®, Dickies®, Scotch & Soda®, Hurley®, Justice®, Bebe®, Elie Tahari®, Limited Too®, Brookstone®, and more—each re-energized through creative vision, strategic partnerships, and a deep understanding of global markets. With more than 600 licensees and a growing network of over 500 branded retail stores across North America, Europe, Australia, South America, India, Asia, the Middle East, and the United Arab Emirates, Bluestar Alliance continues to expand its global presence—most notably through the Bluestar Luxury Group, focused on building the next generation of luxury and lifestyle brands. Bluestar Alliance stands at the intersection of innovation, influence, and brand authority, shaping the future of how consumers experience brands around the world. View source version on businesswire.com: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251112951502/en/ VF Media Colin Wheeler Vice President, Corporate Affairs, Public Relations and Communications corporate_communications@vfc.com VF Investor Relations Allegra Perry Vice President, Investor Relations ir@vfc.com Bluestar Alliance, LLC Sarah Rosen Bluestar Alliance SRosen@Bluestarall.com Source: VF Corporation Released November 12, 2025

title: Odessa Pumps and Sandpiper Partner to Solve Customer's AODD Issues
summary: Odessa Pumps recently teamed up with Sandpiper Pump to support a large composite pipe company that was having failures with their existing AODD pumps.
body_text: Recently, Odessa Pumps was contacted by a large composite pipe company that was having failures with their existing air-operated double diaphragm (AODD) pumps. This customer originally had a pump service life of approximately 1 year before experiencing a diaphragm failure, but they had seen that service life drop to 6 months and then to 3 months. Odessa Pumps teamed up with Sandpiper to support the customer and resolve the shortened diaphragm life problem. Odessa Pumps and Sandpiper conducted a site audit with the customer and concluded that the overall pump system was set up adequately for their application. When the audit’s focus turned to the pump itself, we found that the existing AODD pump’s design had a single PTFE diaphragm, which is highly chemical resistant but susceptible to material fatigue, leading to shortened diaphragm life compared to other materials. Our recommendation was to replace the current AODD pumps with a Sandpiper model designed with a double-layered PTFE diaphragm and Santoprene® TPV backing for additional durability. Since replacing their pumps, the customer has seen their 3-month service life improve to nearly 2 years of service without a diaphragm failure. They have since ordered an additional 2 Sandpiper pumps to replace their other AODD units. About Odessa Pumps Odessa Pumps, a DNOW Company, is a trusted provider of industrial pumping solutions, serving a wide range of industries, including oil and gas, water treatment, chemical processing and more. With a strong focus on customer satisfaction and technical expertise, Odessa Pumps delivers reliable and efficient pumping solutions to meet the unique needs of its customers. Discover more about our offerings on the Odessa Pumps page . About Sandpiper Pump For more than 50 years, SANDPIPER has offered continuous innovation, providing the most reliable and durable air-operated double-diaphragm (AODD) pumps to support an extensive set of markets around the world. Each pump is backed by superior workmanship, expertise and industry-leading durability, performance and delivery. To find out more about this AODD pump manufacturer, visit their website: www.sandpiperpump.com #odessapumps #sandpiper #AODD #pumps

title: Greenfire Resources Announces Launch of Rights Offering and Conditional Notice of Redemption for its Senior Secured Notes due 2028
summary: CALGARY, ALBERTA – November 3, 2025 – Greenfire Resources Ltd. (NYSE: GFR, TSX: GFR) (\"Greenfire\" or the \"Company\"), today announced its intention to undertake a rights offering of its common shares for gross proceeds of approximately C$300 million (the \"Rights Offering\").
body_text: Download PDF CALGARY, ALBERTA – November 6, 2025 – Greenfire Resources Ltd. (NYSE: GFR, TSX: GFR) (“Greenfire” or the “Company”) today confirmed the launch of its previously announced CAD$300 million rights offering (the “ Rights Offering “) and the conditional redemption of its outstanding US$237.5 million aggregate principal amount of 12% senior secured notes due 2028 (the “ 2028 Notes “). The Rights Offering is available to holders of common shares of the Company (the “ Common Shares “) of record as at the close of business on November 17, 2025 (the “ Record Date “). Pursuant to the Rights Offering, each holder of Common Shares as at the Record Date will receive one right (a “ Right “) for each Common Share held. Each Right entitles the holder thereof to subscribe for 0.7849 Common Shares and every 1.2740 Rights entitle an eligible holder to subscribe for one Common Share at a subscription price of either CAD$5.44 or US$3.85 (the “ Subscription Price “). The Subscription Price reflects a 15% discount to Greenfire’s 2-day volume-weighted-average share price as of close of business on November 5, 2025, which reflects the minimum permitted discount for a rights offering under applicable TSX rules. Subject to any further restrictions that a shareholder’s securities broker or dealer, bank or trust company may impose, determination of the Subscription Price currency in Canadian dollars or United States dollars will be at the subscriber’s sole discretion. The Rights Offering includes an additional subscription privilege under which eligible holders of Rights who exercise all of the Rights issued to them under their basic subscription privilege will be entitled to subscribe for additional Common Shares, if available, that are not otherwise subscribed for under the Rights Offering. In connection with the Rights Offering, Greenfire has entered into a standby purchase agreement with certain limited partnerships comprising Waterous Energy Fund (collectively, the “ WEF Shareholders “), (the “ Standby Purchase Agreement “). The WEF Shareholders currently own approximately 55.9% of the Company’s outstanding Common Shares and have agreed, subject to certain terms and conditions, to exercise their basic subscription privilege in full and will, on a proportionate basis to each of the WEF Shareholder’s current Common Share holdings, purchase all of the Common Shares that are not otherwise subscribed for and purchased under the Rights Offering by holders of Rights so that the maximum number of Common Shares issuable under the Rights Offering will be issued and purchased (the “ Standby Commitment “). No standby fee will be paid to the Standby Purchasers in connection with the Rights Offering. The Company expects to raise gross proceeds of approximately $300 million from the Rights Offering and intends to use the proceeds less offering expenses, together with cash on hand, to fund the redemption of the 2028 Notes, as described below. Full details of the Rights Offering are set out in the Rights Offering notice (the “ Rights Offering Notice “) and Rights Offering Circular (the “ Rights Offering Circular “), which are available on the Company’s profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and on EDGAR at www.sec.gov . Concurrently with the launch of the Rights Offering, the Company issued a conditional notice of redemption for the 2028 Notes. The redemption price for the notes is 106.000% of the aggregate outstanding principal amount thereof, plus accrued and unpaid interest, through December 18 , 2025. The redemption date is expected to occur on December 19 , 2025. The redemption of the 2028 Notes is subject to completion of the Rights Offering. In the Company’s discretion, the redemption may not occur and the redemption notice may be rescinded in the event such condition shall not have been satisfied by the redemption date. A statement issued by the rights agent, Odyssey Trust Company, under the direct registration system (“ Rights DRS Advice “) will be mailed to each eligible registered holder of Common Shares as at the Record Date, together with a copy of the Rights Offering Notice. To subscribe for Common Shares issuable under the Rights Offering, registered holders of Common Shares must complete the subscription form attached to the Rights DRS Advice (the “ Subscription Form “) and deliver the Rights DRS Advice and Subscription Form, together with payment of the aggregate Subscription Price (including payment for any subscription pursuant to the additional subscription privilege), by mail to the Rights depositary and subscription agent, Odyssey Trust Company, prior to 4:00 p.m. (the “ Expiry Time “) on December 16, 2025 (the “ Expiry Date “). Shareholders who hold their Common Shares through an intermediary, such as a bank, trust company, securities dealer or broker, will receive materials and instructions from their intermediary. The Rights Offering is being made to all eligible holders of Common Shares as of the Record Date who are resident in any of the provinces of Canada or the United States (the “ Eligible Jurisdictions “). Accordingly, and subject to the detailed provisions of the Rights Offering Circular, Rights will not be delivered to, nor will they be exercisable by, persons resident outside of any of the Eligible Jurisdictions, unless such Rights holder can establish that the exercise of Rights would be lawful and in compliance with all securities and other laws applicable to the Company and the jurisdiction such holder is a resident. The Rights are transferable and will be listed for trading on the TSX at the opening of trading on the Record Date under the symbol “GFR.RT” and will cease trading at 12:00 p.m. (Toronto time) on the Expiry Date. It is expected that the Rights will begin trading on a “When-Issued” basis on the NYSE on November 14, 2025, under the symbol “GFR RTWI” and will begin regular-way trading under symbol “GFR RT” on November 25, 2025. The Rights will cease trading on the NYSE before market open on the Expiry Date. Holders of Rights may sell their Rights through the facilities of the TSX and NYSE. Rights not exercised at or prior to the Expiry Time on the Expiry Date will be void and of no value and will be cancelled. As at the date hereof there are 70,256,512 Common Shares issued and outstanding. The Company expects that following the closing of the Rights Offering there will be 125,403,570 Common Shares issued and outstanding. Related Party Transaction The Rights Offering is not subject to the related party provisions of Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Securityholders in Special Transactions based on a prescribed exception for rights offerings. The terms of the Rights Offering and the entry into the Standby Purchase Agreement on behalf of the Company was considered and approved by a special committee comprised of independent members of the Board of Greenfire with no material interest in the Rights Offering or connection to the WEF Shareholders. This news release does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy nor shall there be any sale of any of the securities in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful. Neither this Rights Offering nor the Rights or Common Shares issuable in connection with this Rights Offering have been approved or disapproved by the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the “ SEC “) or any state securities regulator nor has the SEC or any state securities regulator passed upon the accuracy or adequacy of the Circular. Any representation to the contrary is a criminal offence. The TSX has not reviewed and does not accept responsibility for the adequacy of the content of the information contained herein, and no securities regulatory authority has either approved or disapproved the contents of this news release. This press release is for informational purposes only and does not constitute an offer to buy or the solicitation of an offer to sell with respect to any securities. The Rights and the Common Shares issuable pursuant thereto will be issued by way of the Rights Offering Notice and Rights Offering Circular filed with the securities commission or similar authority in each of the provinces of Canada. The Company has filed a registration statement on Form F-10 (including the Rights Offering Notice and Rights Offering Circular) with the SEC for the Rights Offering to which this news release relates. Before you invest, you should read the Rights Offering Notice and the Rights Offering Circular included in the registration statement on Form F-10 and the other documents that the Company has filed with the SEC for more complete information about the Company and the Rights Offering, especially risk factors relating to the securities offered. Prospective investors may read and download any public document that Greenfire has filed with Canadian securities regulators, including the Rights Offering Notice and Rights Offering Circular, on Greenfire’s profile on the System for Electronic Data Analysis and Retrieval+ (SEDAR+) at www.sedarplus.ca. Greenfire’s registration statement on Form F-10, reports and other information filed by Greenfire with and furnished to the SEC can be read and downloaded on Greenfire’s profile on the SEC’s Electronic Data Gathering and Retrieval (EDGAR) website at www.sec.gov. The Company plans to leverage its large resource base and significant infrastructure in place to drive meaningful, capital-efficient production growth. title: Pure AI-Generated Content Destroys Trust and Engagement. The Remedy Is Human Guidance.
summary: Trust drops 50% when readers suspect pure AI-generated content. The actual key to successful content is a human-guided approach with AI assistance.
body_text: In a Nutshell Reader trust collapses when they suspect AI involvement in your content writing, even when content is actually human-written Unedited AI content degrades performance and destroys trust within months Human-written content delivers quality but cannot meet modern production demands AI-assisted, human-led content delivers superior engagement while maintaining authenticity and allowing you to scale your content strategy Table of Contents The Invisible Conversion Killer: Why Trust Collapses Before Readers Reach Your CTA How Unedited AI-Generated Content Destroys Trust and Conversions Within 3 Months The Human-Written Content Trap: Quality That Cannot Scale AI-Assisted Content Delivers 43% Better Engagement With Sustainable Scale The AI-Assisted Framework: Where AI Excels and Where Humans Must Lead While Competitors Choose Between Quality and Scale, You Can Build Both Frequently Asked Questions The Invisible Conversion Killer: Why Trust Collapses Before Readers Reach Your CTA Your content performs well in Google. Organic traffic looks solid, rankings are climbing. But something invisible is killing conversions before readers reach your CTA. They suspect AI involvement in your content writing. Trust collapses instantly, regardless of whether they're right. Raptive, a digital publishing platform, surveyed 3,000 U.S. adults about AI-generated content perception. When participants suspected content was AI-generated, trust dropped nearly 50 percent . The devastating part: this happened even when content was actually human-written. The study revealed a 14% decrease in purchase consideration when content was perceived as AI-generated. Participants also showed a 14% decrease in willingness to pay premium prices for advertised products. Perhaps most concerning, 52% of consumers disengage from suspected AI-generated content entirely. This is not a quality problem you can fix with better prompts. This is a perception problem that destroys business results. Research across 1.2 million posts and 100+ academic studies reveals a third path: AI-assisted content , where humans lead strategy while AI accelerates research and consistency checking, delivers 43% better engagement than either pure AI or human-only approaches. Research Finding: Raptive's study of 3,000 U.S. adults found: Trust dropped nearly 50 percent when participants suspected AI-generated content (even when actually human-written) Purchase consideration decreased 14% Willingness to pay premium prices dropped 14% AI-Assisted Content Delivers 43% Better Engagement Than Either Extreme Most companies believe they face a binary choice: unedited AI-generated content (cheap, fast, risky) versus human-written content (expensive, slow, quality). Research across 1.2 million posts and 100+ academic studies reveals a third path outperforms both extremes. The Research-Backed Solution: AI-assisted content delivers 43% better engagement than AI-generated or human-written approaches while avoiding AI's 50% trust collapse and human content's economic scale limitations. The solution preserves what makes human content perform (authenticity, strategic positioning and quality judgment) while capturing AI's efficiency advantages in research and consistency. This is not a compromise between quality and speed. This is a systematic approach that outperforms both extremes. Understanding where each approach fails and where AI-assisted strategies succeed determines whether you're building a sustainable content advantage or gambling with your domain authority. The data reveals three distinct paths forward. Unedited AI-Generated Content Is Fast But Trust-Killing This promises speed and cost efficiency but delivers trust erosion and conversion degradation within 3 months. Human-Written Content Delivers Quality But Can't Scale It delivers superior quality metrics (5.44 times more traffic and 41% longer sessions) but cannot meet modern search's volume requirements economically. AI-Assisted Content Delivers the Best of Both Worlds This combines AI's research acceleration with human strategic positioning and quality control, capturing efficiency gains without sacrificing the authenticity that drives conversions. Content Creation Spectrum: What Each Approach Actually Means Category Approach Who's Driving Time Savings vs Human Performance Indicator AI-Generated Content Unedited AI (<5% human) AI generates, publish as-is 77% faster 35% conversion drop after 3 months AI-Generated Content Lightly Edited AI (5-15% human) AI generates, human fixes surface errors ~65% faster "AI stink" still detectable, trust drops 50% Hybrid Content Comprehensively Edited AI (30-50% human) AI creates first draft, human substantially transforms ~45% faster 45% engagement improvement, 28% conversion boost (requires substantial rewriting) Hybrid Content AI-Assisted/ Human-Led (60-80% human) Human creates strategy first, AI assists with execution 40% faster 43% engagement advantage, more efficient workflow throughout Human-Only Content 100% Human Human creates everything Baseline Best quality (41% longer sessions) but 4.3 times slower The Speed Trap: Why 77% Faster Doesn't Mean Better The time savings column reveals why unedited AI-generated content is tempting: producing content 77% faster than human-written approaches promises massive efficiency gains. But speed alone doesn't drive business results. Unedited AI's 16-minute production time delivers a 35% conversion decline and a 50% trust drop over time. Lightly edited, AI-generated content saves time but remains detectable to readers. The AI-assisted content approach captures meaningful time savings ( 40% faster than human-written content ) while maintaining the trust and engagement that drive conversions. You're not choosing between speed and quality; you're choosing between reckless speed (AI-generated) and strategic efficiency (AI-assisted). The Critical Distinction: How Google and Amazon Define AI-Generated vs AI-Assisted Content This distinction is recognized by major platforms like Amazon and Google. AI-generated content: AI creates the initial draft and is classified as AI-generated even after substantial human editing. AI-assisted content: Humans lead the content strategy while AI accelerates research, fact-checking, citation finding, and content optimization. You're not rewriting AI output; you're being assisted throughout the creation process. Both hybrid approaches avoid the trust erosion of lightly edited AI-generated content, but AI-assisted content (where humans lead from the start) enables faster, more sustainable production than comprehensively editing AI drafts. Let's examine what the data reveals about each path, starting with why pure AI content systematically destroys the metrics that matter. How Unedited AI-Generated Content Destroys Trust and Conversions Within 3 Months The "AI Stink" Phenomenon That Destroys Conversions Unedited AI-generated content triggers immediate reader distrust that destroys conversions within months. AI stink, a term gaining traction on Hacker News and Reddit, describes this gut feeling that something was made by AI. Readers have become tuned to specific cues such as tone, phrasing, punctuation and awkward repetition. When Raptive showed participants content and asked if it seemed AI-generated, those who believed it was rated it significantly lower, even when the content was actually human-written. Ads placed next to AI-perceived content suffer measurable damage. The Raptive study showed 17 percent less premium perception , 17% less relatability, and 11% less trustworthiness for advertisements appearing alongside content participants suspected was AI-generated. Raptive explained the business impact: "If your CPM is $5 and performance drops 15%, that loss adds up. That's real money." Your conversion problem might not be your offer. It might be readers sensing AI involvement. Initial Conversions Mask a Systematic Performance Decline Unedited AI pages can show decent initial conversions (2.5-3.5%, slightly above the 2.2% industry average). One AI product review page initially converted at 4.1%, generating $15,000 in monthly revenue. But after 3 months, conversion rates typically dropped 35 percent as bounce rates climbed to 65%. The pattern is consistent: initial visitors may convert, but as users encounter shallow content lacking depth and original insight, they recognize the AI-generated patterns and disengage. Human-written content maintains performance over time. Human-written pages averaged 4.2 minutes of engagement versus 1.8 minutes for AI-generated content. Human-written content showed 18% lower bounce rates and 41% longer session durations. By the Numbers: Unedited AI-generated content typically shows a 35 percent conversion decline after 3 months while bounce rates climb to 65%. Human-written content maintains a 4.2 minutes average time on page versus 1.8 minutes for AI-generated pages. Unedited AI Content at Scale Triggers Google Penalties That Destroy Businesses These conversion and performance degradations are just the beginning. Unedited AI-generated content at scale triggers Google's large-scale content abuse penalty, which can destroy entire businesses within months. Research shows 40 percent of online businesses close down within 6 months of receiving a Google penalty. Only 30% of websites recover rankings within a year. Google's enforcement pattern reveals a consistent threshold: sites with 90%+ unedited AI content face systematic deindexing. The March 2024 Google core update established this pattern when analysis showed 837 websites completely deindexed , erasing over 20.7 million monthly organic visits. Over 50% of deindexed sites had used AI to generate 90-100% of their content. TailRide exemplified this pattern, publishing over 22,000 AI-generated pages in a few months and losing all organic traffic overnight. Their founder's analysis revealed the core problem: "The issue was not AI itself. It was scale plus quality plus trust. The speed made it obvious to Google we were gaming the system." Current Enforcement and Recovery Timelines Enforcement escalated in June 2025 when Google moved from algorithmic filtering to manual review and complete removal from search results. Current tracking shows sites with 90%+ unedited AI content experiencing mass deindexing within 3-6 months of launch. Evidence suggests keeping pure AI-authored content under 30% of total output minimizes risk. Recovery timelines are brutal: manual penalties typically take 10 to 30 days if fixed immediately, while algorithmic penalties generally require 6 months to 2 years for full recovery. This is not a historical problem. This is active enforcement happening right now. Unedited AI-generated content systematically destroys trust, conversions, and search visibility. But human-written content faces the opposite problem. The Human-Written Content Trap: Quality That Cannot Scale Human-written content outperforms AI-generated content on every quality metric that matters. These pages generate 5.44 times more traffic over time . They deliver 41% longer session durations and show 18% lower bounce rates. Users stay engaged: 4.2 minutes on page versus 1.8 minutes for AI-generated content. Analytics platform Hotjar ran a 6-month experiment comparing AI-generated and human-written content performance. The results were stark: human-written content received 39 times more clicks than AI-generated content (4,550 total clicks versus 116). The human-written approach earned 124,000 impressions while AI-generated content managed only 10,800. Average click-through rate told the same story: 3.7% versus 1.1%. Why does authentic, human-crafted content win? Authenticity resonates with readers. Emotional depth drives engagement. Trust matters, especially in finance, health, and legal sectors where 91% of consumers rely on reviews to evaluate businesses. By the Numbers: Human-written content generates 5.44 times more traffic , delivers 41% longer session durations, and shows 18% lower bounce rates compared to unedited AI-generated content. 69 Minutes vs 16 Minutes: Why Production Cost Gaps Push Companies Toward Risky Shortcuts Human-written content typically takes 69 minutes to produce per article versus 16 minutes for unedited AI-generated content on average. That represents 4.3 times longer production time, which translates directly to 4.3 times higher cost. For budget-conscious companies, that cost difference significantly impacts annual content production capacity. Modern SEO Demands Volume Human Teams Cannot Deliver Modern SEO demands volume: competitors are publishing daily, algorithms favor fresh content, and comprehensive topic coverage requires both depth and breadth. The math does not work. Quality content at human speed and human cost cannot meet the volume requirements modern organic search demands. Key Insight: The production time gap of 69 minutes versus 16 minutes explains why scale pressures push companies toward risky AI-only approaches that ultimately destroy trust and conversions. Most companies conclude that they must choose between expensive human quality OR cheap AI volume. Both extremes lose. Unedited AI-generated content destroys trust and conversions. Human-written content production cannot achieve the necessary scale. Human-written content delivers quality while AI-only approaches deliver speed. The data shows you can have both, but only through systematic AI-assisted implementation. AI-Assisted Content With Human Guidance Delivers 43% Better Engagement With Sustainable Scale Social media management platform Buffer analyzed 1.2 million posts across 7 platforms (Facebook, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads, TikTok, Twitter, YouTube). The sample included 15,000 users who created both AI-assisted AND non-AI-generated posts. This controls for user quality because the same creators used both approaches. The results showed AI-assisted advantages across all platforms. Research Finding: Buffer's analysis of 1.2 million posts found that AI-assisted content achieved a 5.87 percent engagement rate versus a 4.82% engagement rate for human-written posts, with consistent improvements across all major platforms. AI-assisted content showed engagement advantages across every social platform tested. Impact varied by platform: Threads showed a 99% increase (11.11% vs. 5.56%), TikTok 47%, Facebook 25%, X/Twitter 32%, Pinterest 13%, while YouTube and LinkedIn showed more modest gains (5% and 10% respectively). Why does AI-assisted content outperform human-written posts when unedited AI-generated content underperforms? This is AI-assisted, not AI-generated content. Humans set the strategy while AI handles the optimization. Consistent production volume creates more engagement opportunities while maintaining quality standards. Digital marketing agency NP Digital's report showed the AI-assisted model boosts content output by 40 percent while safeguarding human creativity. AI-assisted campaigns achieved 43 percent better engagement than AI-generated or human-written efforts. Companies with systematic human oversight reported 67 percent better content performance , experiencing 45% fewer brand consistency issues with human guidance. Teams reported up to 5 times faster production cycles with AI-assisted approaches. One SaaS company replaced half their blog pipeline with an AI plus editor model. They achieved a 12 percent increase in organic clicks over 6 months while maintaining stable conversion rates. In contrast, their unedited AI-generated content experienced the typical 35% conversion decline. The AI-assisted approach also delivered higher lifetime value per visitor and stronger search rankings compared to unedited AI content. By the Numbers: AI-assisted campaigns show 43 percent better engagement than either extreme. Companies with systematic human oversight report 67 percent better content performance and achieve 40 percent increases in output velocity . The 1+1=3 Effect Appears Across All Studies MIT reviewed 100+ studies on human-AI collaboration. The finding: human-AI collaboration holds the most promise for creating high-quality content efficiently . Human-AI combinations performed better on content creation tasks than on decision-making tasks because generative AI enables iterative collaboration. Writers can provide strategic direction, review AI-generated research or initial drafts, and refine outputs in real time. This interactive process allows humans to guide AI assistance throughout content development rather than choosing between full automation or manual creation. Research across multiple domains quantifies this collaboration advantage. One study examining classification tasks found there was a 90 percent accuracy with the human-AI collaborative approach versus 81% for human-only or 73% for AI-only approaches. The 1+1=3 effect emerges when each party contributes something distinctive and valuable. AI processes vast datasets and maintains consistency. Humans provide strategic judgment and authentic voice. Key Insight: The human-AI collaborative approach achieved 90 percent accuracy versus 81% for human-only or 73% for AI-only . This combination outperforms either party working alone. Understanding where AI excels and where humans must lead determines whether your AI-assisted implementation captures these advantages or simply creates expensive inefficiency. The Human Guidance Framework: Where AI Excels and Where Humans Must Lead The performance advantages of AI-assisted content depend on understanding what each party does best. AI excels at processing vast amounts of data, maintaining consistency at scale, and handling repetitive tasks that drain human creativity. Humans excel at strategic positioning, authentic voice, and quality judgment that builds trust. Success comes from systematic division of responsibilities that leverages each party's unique strengths. AI Excels at Research, Consistency, and Creative Acceleration Research and Data Processing at Scale AI pulls citations (references to source material supporting specific claims) in seconds that would take humans hours to find. AI analyzes vast datasets humans cannot process efficiently, examining thousands of keywords for patterns and reviewing 100+ sources simultaneously. Research time drops from days to hours with AI assistance. Marketing agencies report a 40 percent reduction in content production time after adopting AI tools. They also see a 25% reduction in editing time through AI-powered grammar and consistency checking. Research Finding: Marketing agencies report a 40% reduction in content production time and a 25% reduction in editing time with AI-assisted workflows. Real-Time Consistency and Brand Voice Maintenance AI maintains brand voice consistency with infinite recall, never forgetting a guideline while checking every line of copy. Real-time voice and tone compliance checking across all content prevents drift from established standards. Dense text can be instantly transformed into readable, well-formatted documents. Consistent terminology is maintained across millions of words, ensuring that key concepts are described the same way throughout all content. Cross-platform formatting consistency ensures LinkedIn posts, blog articles, and email campaigns maintain message alignment. Key Insight: AI's infinite recall combined with real-time checking enables consistency at scale that humans cannot match. AI never forgets style guidelines while checking every line against established standards. Creative Acceleration Without Creative Control An academic study called AIdeation worked with 16 professional designers to test how AI assistance affects creative work. The research showed AI significantly enhanced both creativity and ideation efficiency , with results showing strong statistical significance. AI helps designers overcome creative blocks and challenge their own assumptions during the ideation process. title: TriMas Enters into Agreement to Sell TriMas Aerospace
summary: Download Press Release BLOOMFIELD HILLS, Michigan, November 4, 2025 – TriMas (NASDAQ: TRS) announced today that it has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Aerospace segment for an all-cash purchase price of approximately $1.45 billion to...
body_text: Download Press Release BLOOMFIELD HILLS, Michigan, November 4, 2025 – TriMas (NASDAQ: TRS) announced today that it has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Aerospace segment for an all-cash purchase price of approximately $1.45 billion to an affiliate of Tinicum L.P. (the “Transaction”). Funds managed by Blackstone will be a minority investor in the Transaction. The purchase price represents an enterprise value multiple of approximately 18x last twelve months (LTM) third quarter 2025 adjusted EBITDA(1). “As previously communicated, the TriMas Board of Directors has been actively evaluating strategic options to optimize our business portfolio and unlock greater value for our shareholders,” commented Herbert Parker, TriMas’ Board of Directors Chair. “We are pleased to announce this agreement, which we believe represents a compelling valuation and validates the strength of the aerospace business we’ve built. Over the past several years, our aerospace leadership team has executed a significant transformation, delivering sustained sales growth, deepening customer partnerships and driving meaningful operational improvements. This transaction reflects the high-quality nature of the business and its continued strong momentum.” “This transaction represents a win for our employees, our shareholders and the future of our business,” said Thomas Snyder, TriMas President & Chief Executive Officer. “Upon completion of this divestiture, we will be centered around a more focused, high-margin packaging platform that will enable us to capitalize on long-term growth and deliver superior value. Our top priority is reinvesting to drive profitable growth, including through targeted high-quality acquisitions. In support of that, we’ve established a Strategic Investment Committee, which will guide disciplined evaluation and prioritization of potential acquisitions that best align with our growth strategy. This committee will also actively evaluate additional options, including returning capital to shareholders and strengthening our balance sheet.” The closing is expected to occur by the end of the first quarter of 2026, subject to customary regulatory approvals and closing conditions. PJT Partners and BofA Securities are serving as financial advisors and have led the sale process, while Jones Day is serving as outside legal counsel for TriMas. Solomon Partners acted as financial advisor to the Purchaser. Kirkland & Ellis served as legal counsel to Takeoff Buyer, Inc. and to Blackstone, while Goodwin Procter advised Tinicum. “We would like to thank the TriMas Aerospace team for its contributions to TriMas and its leadership throughout the sale process. We are also extremely proud of the great work our broader team has done to strengthen and improve its business, and we remain committed to delivering the highest level of service to TriMas Aerospace customers during this transition,” concluded Snyder. About TriMas TriMas designs and manufactures a diverse set of products primarily for the consumer products, aerospace and industrial markets through its TriMas Packaging, TriMas Aerospace and Specialty Products groups. Our approximately 3,900 dedicated employees in 13 countries provide customers with a wide range of innovative and quality product solutions through our market-leading businesses. TriMas is publicly traded on the NASDAQ under the ticker symbol “TRS,” and is headquartered in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan. For more information, please visit www.trimas.com . About TriMas Aerospace TriMas Aerospace is a leading provider of highly-engineered fasteners and precision-machined components for mission-critical applications across the global commercial aerospace and defense industries. Backed by a portfolio of trusted brands, including Monogram Aerospace Fasteners™, Allfast Fastening Systems®, Mac Fasteners™, TFI Aerospace, TriMas Aerospace Germany, Martinic Engineering™, RSA Engineered Products™ and Weldmac Manufacturing Company, TriMas Aerospace delivers innovative solutions that meet the most rigorous industry standards. With approximately $374 million in revenue over the last twelve months, the business operates nine manufacturing facilities and employs around 1,250 dedicated team members, all focused on supporting the evolving needs of aerospace customers worldwide. general economic and currency conditions; competitive factors; market demand; our ability to realize our business strategies; government and regulatory actions, including, without limitation, the impact of current and future tariffs and reciprocal tariffs, quotas and surcharges, as well as climate change legislation and other environmental regulations; the disruption of operations from catastrophic or extraordinary events, including, but not limited to, natural disasters, geopolitical conflicts and public health crises; the amount and timing of future dividends and/or share repurchases, which remain subject to Board approval and depend on market and other conditions; our future prospects; and other risks that are discussed in Part I, Item 1A, "Risk Factors," in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, and Part II, Item 1A, "Risk Factors," in our subsequent Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q. title: AI & Affiliate Monitoring: How Modern Tools Detect Rules & Policy Violations (2025)
body_text: TLDR; Artificial Intelligence is transforming compliance by automating the tedious, error-prone work of monitoring affiliates, disclosures, and brand mentions across every channel. Affil.ai’s AI-driven platform replaces static rule-based checks with contextual analysis that detects real violations, reduces false positives, and keeps brands aligned with complex regulations. Just as the Space Race of the 20th century sparked inventions far beyond rockets, like memory foam and medical imaging, the modern race for dominance in Artificial Intelligence is igniting breakthroughs that reshape everyday industries. Algorithms and automation are finally replacing decades of manual, error-prone monitoring with smarter, faster, and more scalable AI-driven solutions. Affil.ai was founded on the recognition that innovative applications of AI could transform how brands handle affiliate monitoring & compliance. This article dives into how AI is reshaping the compliance landscape across industries, and how Affil is leading that transformation through the combination of multiple AI capabilities. Affil aims to steadily eliminate the pain points of compliance, which has been a persistent challenge for brands, regardless of sector. How can AI technology be implemented in compliance? Amongst AI’s greatest strengths are its ability to automate repetitive tasks, detect patterns with precision, and handle massive volumes of data. All the aforementioned strengths are conducive to conducting impeccable compliance monitoring. Below are several ways Affil deploys AI technology to modernize the compliance process from end-to-end. (1) Crawling vs. Manual Submission Traditional compliance monitoring is preceded by affiliates submitting content for review to compliance teams. The problem with this anachronistic process is twofold: (1) it relies on affiliates to manually submit every piece of content for review (leaving room for human error); and (2) content distributed through sub-affiliates (or other third party actors) may pervert brand image and increase compliance risks. Addressing (1), Affil lifts the burden from affiliates and brands’ compliance teams with an advanced web-crawling technology that scans affiliate sites, with the ability to scan hundreds of affiliate pages within minutes. Addressing (2), Affil’s solution can map an entire affiliate network , identifying sub-affiliates and/or third-party content that republish or alter affiliate content. (2) Hidden content: drop-downs, side bars, and carousels Modern online content unintentionally hides information through collapsibles, dynamic carousels, interactive tables, etc. Affil can detect any and all content that is not readily visible or only available once triggered by users, ensuring that all information in these elements are reviewed like a static document. This means no hidden content will slip through the cracks. (2) Social Media The scope of compliance monitoring in the modern age far exceeds web-based content. Affiliates are no longer just blog publishers, but also influencers, creators, and artists. Accordingly, the multiplicity of marketing channels add an additional complexity by increasing the scope of monitoring to various social media channels such as Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok. Affil’s compliance solution can analyze social media captions, hashtags, and even video overlays. The product combines AI-powered product detection and analysis with optical character recognition (OCR) technology to detect compliance issues such as missing disclosures or inaccurate representations of the brand. This synergic combination ensures reliable oversight across every marketing channel, not just owned web-based written blogs. (3) Snapshots: the modern wayback machine Compliance’s requisite for record keeping (and in turn manual documentation) is another pain point for compliance review. Compliance teams need a reliable source of truth for content that’s live today, but was also live last week, to maintain a defensible audit trail. Affil’s snapshot capabilities capture point-in-time versions of content throughout marketing channels, allowing brands to review historical versions of a singular piece of content. This capability can be thought of as a modern “ Wayback Machine ” for affiliate record keeping, ensuring that even deleted or edited posts are fully documented for the brand to review. (4) Proactive, pre-published solutions The future of compliance is proactive , not reactive. Affil integrates an AI-reviewer into its compliance solution, which is trained on both regulatory and brand guidelines. The AI-reviewer then scans affiliate content prior to publishing, allowing compliance teams to start the risk mitigation process prior to content being live to the public. This proactive approach means fewer takedowns, fewer communication between the brand and affiliates, and more confidence that every set of public-facing content aligns with brand and regulatory standards. Is AI compliance limited to certain industries? As long as there are clear requirements, AI compliance has the ability to adapt to any industry’s unique policies. While there are broad corollaries across the board (eg ensuring clear & transparent advertising disclosures, as noted by FTC guidelines), at the end of the day, requirements aren’t really too different from one another. While a credit card has annual fees and a pharmaceutical product has indications, these are just “product information” that are binary true or false. Finance Sector Regulatory enforcements continue to be unpredictable and complex. With products such as cryptocurrency and BNPL products, the regulatory environment is still unknown. For highly regulated areas such as credit card marketing, Affil has cemented a strong foothold in monitoring brand activity and remediate issues. We have developed the only solution that bridges regulatory guidelines like TILA/Regulation Z alongside ensuring product information like APRs are accurate. Likewise, for banking, we can also easily detect the presence of required disclosures. For example, when fintech banking products that work with a partner bank mention deposit insurance, they must display a full disclosure on the page that these products are not insured by the FDIC. Current methods to check this are extremely manual and tedious; however, Affil’s AI has the full functionality to detect these scenarios. Affil offers a solution that your company can use for risk mitigation, in preparation for a new age of unpredictable regulations. Pharma Sector Ensuring your marketing content accurately reflects indications or adverse events can be tricky. Affiliates or other third party marketing partners are not going to use the verbatim language when describing product usage. For example, a pharmaceutical company promoting a drug like Ozempic® must ensure that any mention of benefits—such as glucose control or weight loss—is balanced with reference to potential adverse events like nausea, vomiting, or pancreatitis. However, without AI, the only way to truly scan for this type of language is via manual efforts. If you’re looking for a solution to monitor for language that should or shouldn’t be mentioned in pharmaceutical advertising, then Affil can offer a strong solution for you. Insurance Sector In the insurance industry, compliance and disclosure accuracy are paramount. Whether it’s life, health, or property coverage, marketing materials must clearly outline policy limitations, exclusions, and terms of eligibility. However, third-party publishers or affiliates often paraphrase or omit critical disclosures such as “coverage not available in all states” or “subject to underwriting approval.” Affil’s AI disclosure detection has the unique ability to detect a wide variety of disclosures on pages, including custom ones to the insurance sector. By automating these reviews, insurance marketers can reduce regulatory risk and maintain brand integrity. What types of rules can AI compliance handle? AI compliance has the ability to ingest and understand a wide variety of compliance situations. On one end, AI compliance can easily handle incorrect product information. Let’s say you’re advertising a BNPL product; you’re going to want your marketing materials to accurately reflect how it works. Late fees, interest rates, and financing terms are just some of the information you’re going to want to be correct. On the other end are what we refer to as “guidelines” related issues. For example, from the credit card industry, let’s say that affiliates are required to list a Rates & Fees link adjacent to trigger terms like APRs, annual fees, and late fees to comply with Regulation Z/TILA . Affil’s AI compliance has the ability to essentially detect if statements and paragraphs are meeting this requirement. How does this differ from BrandVerity’s policy monitoring? With solutions like BrandVerity, the biggest problem is that you are setting static “policies” that are purely looking for the presence of the words. There is no AI behind the scene; rather, it just searches your content for that particular keyword. For starters, to do any type of monitoring or compliance requires tools to accurately detect the product names. If you are only looking for mentions of your brand’s unique terms (eg “Scrub Daddy”), then BrandVerity will do a fantastic job, since the use case of the term is rather unique to the beloved sponge. However, if your product is something like “ Ramp ” or “Chase,” you’re going to run into a ton of false positives purely when it comes to product identification. Next, when it comes to actually executing compliance, BrandVerity does not have the ability to deeply differentiate between multiple products on a page. A common pain point we encountered at Affil was in regards to credit card listicles—these are very common credit card comparison pages that would list 10+ credit cards on the same page. While your BrandVerity rule might be looking to identify any outdated annual fees for Card ABC, it has no ability to differentiate between Card ABC and XYZ, leading to a tremendous amount of false positives. Affil does not struggle with this because AI-based rules are able to take in full context of pages. How does this differ from PerformLine’s AI marketing compliance? PerformLine also struggles with the same “static” rules that BrandVerity has. With their product detection, it’s not possible to provide context on product names, so you’ll run into many false positives if your brand uses a “common” word (eg “Lemonade” will trigger many incorrect pages). In terms of the actual marketing compliance itself, the biggest gap is that PerformLine wasn’t built with AI at its core infrastructure. In essence, PerformLine was one of the top marketing monitoring solutions in the 2010s; however, their solution right now lacks true AI integration, which means it suffers from many similar problems as BrandVerity when it comes to accurate issue detection. If your compliance software creates more violations than the amount of content you have to monitor, you aren’t really saving time. Why is AI crucial for brand monitoring & compliance? AI is the only way to give the appropriate context and information to properly determine brand mentions and run compliance. Without AI, you’d need to essentially create hard set rules to capture every compliance situation, which is simply impossible to do. If you want to derisk your external, third party marketing channels using AI, let’s talk!
